best_idea: Give each rig layer its own thread with a signal mask, so a new state (aim, stop, dance) cancels only the layers it owns, and stretch one keyframe clip by ground speed so the leg cadence follows the speed.
decision_why: Take the thread-and-mask model and the speed-scaled keyframe clip for the hero rig, but round the frame count instead of truncating, and never clear an aim flag in the restore thread's first statement; the rig only shows engine state.
acceptance: A player sees the hero's leg cadence quicken and slow with ground speed (2 to 8 frames per keyframe), and after an aim the arms hold 3 s then return; a client test asserts a 4-frame keyframe lasts 4 frames and the aim flag stays true for the whole hold.
